purpose: Four collection/counting/ranking problems as eight Korean/English manuscripts with complete runnable solutions and bounded exhaustive checks.

previousPR.deploymentVerification: Recorded outside repository after production deployment.

newEnglishEditions.policy: After explicit approval refresh the four first-English publishedAt/updatedAt timestamps before final CI; preserve Korean original publication dates and reviewed bodies.

selectionEvidence.purpose: Complete a coherent stack/frequency/ranking/distinct-count group after the prior Java batch.
selectionEvidence.limits: No claim of measured English search demand for these four topics.

sourceVerification.checked: Primary problem conditions and Java contracts checked; long copied stories replaced with concise paraphrases.

review.type: Two-pass self AI review: source/code/English-Korean meaning, then each edition as a standalone article.
review.scope: Eight manuscripts, complete paired source classes, regression fixture scope, original identities and generated HTML.

findings.issue: Original pair deletion example used boxed Character variables with reference comparison and legacy Stack. ASCII inputs happened to satisfy cache assumptions.
findings.resolution: Use ArrayDeque and primitive char comparison; explain the prefix invariant and unboxing, test repeated and alternating million-character inputs.

findings.issue: Old copied descriptions and partial methods obscured the reasoning and runnable context.
findings.resolution: Provide concise constraints, full Solution classes/imports, stack/count/selection proofs and ratio example.

findings.issue: Runner joined all positive map keys instead of making the one-missing-person contract explicit.
findings.resolution: Count duplicates and return the single count1 entry; explain order independence and that fallback exception is not complete validation.

findings.issue: Exact ratio comparison introduces products beyond int bounds.
findings.resolution: Use long count arrays and products, zero-rate denominator1, and stage-number tie break; test200000players/500stages.

findings.issue: Initial stack prose said every character was pushed once.
findings.resolution: State at most once for push and pop.

execution.compilerAndRuntime: JDK17.0.8.1 with javac --release11; no separate JDK11 runtime tested.

runnerScenarios.reference: Known omitted position; completion order reversed. Scenarios are not deduplicated by resulting arrays.

failureScenarios.reference: Independent full population scans for reached counts, sharing exact ratio mathematics with the solution.

pokemonArrays.reference: Enumerate all selections of N/2 positions rather than reuse min(distinct,slots).

otherChecks: One million alternating letters plus retained one million repeated letters
All users completed or later stages unreachable
limits: Problem contracts, not general invalid-input validators
Eight identical bilingual code pairs checked once at runtime; not independent implementation or human review

siteValidation.eightPageAudit: Passed H1/descriptions/OG/BlogPosting dates, canonical/self and reciprocal en/ko/x-default, RSS/search/sitemap lastmod, full code and no editorial banners.

ci: Existing mandatory test:articles step now checks eight paired articles and expanded boundaries; exact PR result tracked separately.
publication: Draft review only; no new batch content deployed before explicit approval.
